panels.title: Oldest open request
panels.description: Age since submission, not time in the current status. Read the request progress row to identify the delayed stage.

panels.title: Extract tasks completed / sec
panels.description: Committed completions. Read alongside backlog, failures and active chunks; zero can mean an empty queue.

panels.title: Extract task failures
panels.description: Failed + error outcomes divided by completed + failed + error. Unavailable claims are excluded. No outcomes or missing telemetry shows No data.

panels.title: HTTP server errors
panels.description: Backend HTTP 5xx share. Zero traffic is not evidence of availability.

panels.title: Slots holding chunks
panels.description: Share of configured slots currently holding claimed work, including I/O and persistence. This is occupancy, not CPU utilization.

panels.title: Longest pool wait
panels.description: Worst PgBouncer client wait across poolers. Open the pooling row to identify the affected clients.

targets.expr: 100 * max(max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"geoquery-db-.*"}) / max by (namespace, persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"geoquery-db-.*"}))

panels.title: Fullest database volume
panels.description: Filesystem usage on the fullest database PVC. Thin-provisioned Ceph pool capacity must also be checked in storage monitoring.

panels.title: Scrape targets failing
panels.description: Currently discovered targets failing their scrape. Disappeared targets are covered separately by deployment readiness and target counts.
Current open requests by stage, including custom-boundary ingestion. Empty stages report zero only when the database query succeeds.
panels.title: Open Requests by Status

panels.description: Age since submission of the oldest open request currently in each stage, not residence time in that stage. Zero means no requests in that stage; missing data remains a gap.
panels.title: Oldest Open Request by Stage
Submission to Output Completion
panels.description: Time from submission to committed output completion, including queuing and extraction. Observed on completion, so use oldest-open-request age for unfinished work. Retries/rebuilds can yield another observation; manual commands without a metrics endpoint are excluded.

panels.title: Request Outcomes in the Trailing Hour
panels.description: Committed terminal transitions. A failed notification after output completion records both completed and failed; retried requests can appear again. These are events, not distinct requests.

panels.title: Requests Currently Failed
panels.description: Current failed requests awaiting intervention or reset. This is a gauge, not the rate of new failures.

POST /api/analytics/requests/ — submitting an extraction request. Pinned to POST because GET on this view name returns 404 by design; those instant responses would otherwise drag the percentiles down. Custom-boundary submissions ingest up to CUSTOM_BOUNDARY_MAX_FEATURES (default 100k) synchronously inside the request, so the tail here is upload size, not queue depth.

targets.expr:
# P50 - median response time
histogram_quantile(0.50,
  sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", view="request-list-create", method="POST"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le)
) * 1000

# P95 - captures most user experience
histogram_quantile(0.95,
  sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", view="request-list-create", method="POST"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le)
) * 1000

# P99 - tail latency for SLO tracking
histogram_quantile(0.99,
  sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", view="request-list-create", method="POST"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le)
) * 1000

panels.title: Request Creation Latency (POST)

panels.description: Extract tasks created by the builder and request materialization compared with completed tasks. Completions above creation indicate depletion of existing work; creation above completions indicates accumulation, assuming other state changes are negligible. Workers can remain fully occupied while draining a large backlog. Builder starvation requires additional evidence of low pending work and elevated slot idle time.
panels.title: Tasks Created vs Completed per Hour

panels.description: Vacuum-lagged partial-index estimates, on a logarithmic scale. Use the separate failed-task panel for small error counts. These are not exact counts or a reliable completion ETA.
panels.title: Pending and In-Flight Tasks (estimated)
Errored Extract Tasks (estimated)
panels.description: Estimated errored tasks, displayed on a linear scale so failures are not hidden by millions of pending tasks. Refreshed by vacuum/analyze.

Extract task outcomes per second across processing workers. Completed and failed outcomes are counted after the persistence transaction commits. Unavailable means the claimed row was no longer running or its dataset, processing option or boundary was deactivated; error means an exception before the row was loaded.
panels.title: Extract Tasks/sec by Outcome
Extract Failure Percentage
panels.description: Failed and error outcomes divided by completed, failed and error outcomes. Unavailable is shown separately in the outcome chart. No outcomes produces a gap.

panels.title: Oldest Active Chunk vs Reaper Deadline
panels.description: Age of currently unfinished chunks, sampled live from worker slots. Cleared on completion or detected child death. A chunk can be reclaimed after the configured deadline; the reaper runs periodically. Dead pods are detected through scrape health and readiness.

Wall time from claiming a chunk of extract tasks to finishing or releasing all of it. The chunk's rows sit in status 2 that long, and free_stale_processing_tasks returns them to pending after STALE_TASK_MINUTES (30), after which they run twice. Yellow from 15 minutes, red from 25: lower the processing claimBatch before it gets there. max is the upper bound of the highest bucket that saw a chunk. Only finished/released chunks are observed; use Oldest Active Chunk for currently hung work. Histogram quantiles above the largest finite bucket cannot resolve the true duration.
panels.title: Finished Chunk Duration
Worker Process Deaths in the Trailing Hour
panels.description: Abrupt extract-worker child-process deaths (such as OOM kills or segfaults) detected by the parent, per pod, over the trailing hour. The parent replaces the process; unresolved tasks wait for the stale-task reaper. This counter does not cover loss of the entire pod. increase() handles counter resets and can produce fractional estimates.

panels.title: Persistence Retries and Exhausted Batches
panels.description: Trailing hour. Connection failures retry persistence without recomputing. Exhausted batches release unresolved claims; these events can occur without a failed task outcome.

Worker slots, by what they are doing: running tasks, claiming the next chunk (claim lock wait and claim), or idle between chunks (including the wait after finding the queue empty). The stack should come to roughly the fleet's slot count (replicas × concurrency); a shortfall is time none of these cover, such as releasing a chunk, closing connections, or worker processes being recycled. Configured slots is the live capacity reference, exported by each worker parent. Work is observed after completion, so short windows can lag current occupancy.
panels.title: Where Slot Time Goes

panels.description: Mean active wall time per finished task, split by phase; time waiting in the result buffer is excluded. lock = read the already-claimed row; load = resource, geometry and category-map lookups; extract = raster I/O and compute; write = build result rows plus an equal share of the batch DELETE and COPY; finalize = an equal share of the claim recheck, status update and commit, including deferred foreign-key checks. Flush retries are included. Before 2026-10-03, write included the recheck and used a multi-row INSERT, so it is not comparable across that change.
panels.title: Mean Seconds per Task by Phase

panels.description: Fraction of each phase's wall time spent on CPU in the worker process. Low means the phase is waiting on the database or disk; near 100% means it is compute-bound.
panels.title: CPU Share per Phase

panels.description: Fraction of time the fleet-wide claim lock is held by a processing worker's claim. Near 100%, the claim is the throughput ceiling and more slots will only add lock wait; raise claimBatch so each claim takes more tasks. The dashed line marks 90%, above which the claim is likely limiting throughput.
panels.title: Claim Lock Utilization

panels.description: Time a worker waits to acquire the fleet-wide claim lock, including any wait for a pooler connection.
panels.title: Claim Lock Wait

panels.description: Time a worker process waits between finishing one chunk and claiming the next. Normally near zero; a slot that found the queue empty waits about EXTRACT_WORKER_IDLE_SECONDS (60s by default) before claiming again.
panels.title: Slot Idle Gap

panels.description: Datasets completing the most extract tasks per second. Picked per point, so more than ten can appear over a long range.
panels.title: Completed Tasks/sec – Top 10 Datasets
Processing Worker Replicas
panels.description: Desired, current and available pods. HPA desired appears only when autoscaling is enabled. Desired above available indicates scheduling/startup/rollout trouble, not necessarily an extraction bottleneck.

panels.title: Application Pods Unavailable
panels.description: Unavailable replicas across application Deployments, including services without their own metrics endpoint. A deleted Deployment disappears; compare expected deployment inventory when diagnosing missing services.

panels.title: CPU Used by Pod
panels.description: CPU cores consumed across application containers in each pod. Processing workers have requests but no CPU limit by default.

targets.expr: 100 * sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"(processing-worker|background-worker|backend|geoquery-db)-.*", container!="", container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pod) (rate(container_cpu_cfs_periods_total{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"(processing-worker|background-worker|backend|geoquery-db)-.*", container!="", container!="POD"}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: CPU Throttled Periods
panels.description: Share of CFS periods throttled. Missing/zero denominators are gaps; unlimited containers may have no series. This is not percentage of CPU time lost.

panels.title: Memory Working Set by Pod
panels.description: Working-set memory, including all application containers. Use container memory limits alongside this chart; processing workers have no limit by default.

targets.expr: 100 * max by (namespace,pod,container) (container_memory_working_set_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"(processing-worker|background-worker|backend|geoquery-db)-.*", container!="", container!="POD"}) / on(namespace,pod,container) (max by (namespace,pod,container) (kube_pod_container_resource_limits{namespace=~"$namespace", pod=~"(processing-worker|background-worker|backend|geoquery-db)-.*", resource="memory", unit="byte"}) > 0)

panels.title: Container Memory vs Limit
panels.description: Only containers with a positive memory limit are shown. Unlimited workers remain visible in the absolute-memory chart.

panels.title: Container Restarts in the Trailing Hour
panels.description: Container restarts; complements extract child-process deaths. Entire pod replacements start new series and may not increment this counter.

panels.title: Time Since a Background Job Returned Successfully
panels.description: Latest normal return across background pods. No successful run since startup yields no series here; see the never-succeeded panel. A normal return can still include handled item failures. Builder workers can run for hours; compare useful work and duration, not just freshness.

panels.title: Jobs with No Successful Run Since Pod Startup
panels.description: 1 means no currently scraped background pod has seen this job return normally. Event-driven ingestion/materialization jobs can legitimately remain at 1 until used. This is distinct from missing exporter data.

panels.title: Background Job Results per Hour
panels.description: Completed job invocations. Error means an exception escaped; handled item errors are reflected in request outcomes and builder batch failures. Abrupt process death cannot report a finished invocation.

panels.title: Background Job P95 Duration
panels.description: Finished invocation durations. The global builder may run for hours and only records duration on return; its live progress is the tasks-created counter.

panels.title: Background Work in the Trailing Hour
panels.description: Committed builder task inserts, reclaimed stale tasks, completed request outputs, and handled builder batch errors. Builder progress increments after each batch, not only when its long-running job finishes.

Tasks published and waiting for a worker to pick them up. A flat non-zero line on background means the queue is not draining. RabbitMQ reports a queue only from the node hosting it, so this is a max across nodes rather than a sum. Extract tasks no longer go through RabbitMQ, so processing stays empty.
panels.title: Celery Queue Depth (Ready)

panels.description: Messages delivered to a consumer but not yet acknowledged. The background worker uses early acknowledgements, so executing tasks have already been acknowledged while prefetched, reserved tasks remain here. This measures outstanding deliveries, not running tasks or concurrency in use; a busy worker can show zero.
panels.title: Celery Messages Delivered but Unacknowledged

panels.description: Broker consumers subscribed to each queue. A prefork Celery worker subscribes through its parent process, so this does not count execution slots or scale with its child-process concurrency. Dropping to zero means nothing is subscribed to serve that queue.
panels.title: Celery Consumers per Queue

targets.expr: 100 * max by (persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_used_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"geoquery-db-.*"}) / max by (persistentvolumeclaim) (kubelet_volume_stats_capacity_bytes{namespace=~"$namespace", persistentvolumeclaim=~"geoquery-db-.*"})

panels.title: Database Volume Fill
panels.description: Filesystem fill per database PVC, including WAL. Does not represent remaining physical capacity in a shared thin-provisioned storage pool.

panels.title: Database Volume Available Space
panels.description: Space available on each database filesystem. Check Ceph pool capacity separately before expansion.

panels.title: Replica Replay Lag
panels.description: Primary-observed recent WAL replay delay. Pair with byte lag and receiver health: time lag alone can be zero or absent when idle/disconnected.

panels.title: Replica WAL Yet to Replay
panels.description: Difference between primary WAL position and connected replica replay position. A disconnected replica disappears here; check WAL receiver health.

panels.title: Replica WAL Receiver Up
panels.description: 1 means the replica has a WAL receiver process; 0 means it does not. This is a liveness signal, not proof of freshness.

targets.expr: sum by (pod) (increase(cnpg_pg_stat_database_conflicts{namespace=~"$namespace", datname="app"}[1h]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 1))

panels.title: Replica Query Cancellations in the Trailing Hour
panels.description: Queries cancelled due to conflicts with recovery. A rising count can explain replica-backed API failures even with low replay lag.

panels.title: Age of Latest Successful Backup
panels.description: Barman Cloud plugin timestamp, exposed through CNPG. No data means backup metrics are unavailable, backups are disabled, or no successful backup exists; it is not a healthy zero. Thresholds assume the chart default twice-daily schedule.

panels.title: Backup Failure Newer Than Latest Success
panels.description: 1 means the most recent reported failure is newer than the latest successful backup; 0 means it is not. Missing plugin metrics remain missing.

panels.title: WAL Archiving Failures in the Trailing Hour
panels.description: Failed archive attempts. Read with archive backlog; retries can later succeed.

panels.title: WAL Segments Awaiting Archive
panels.description: WAL files marked ready for archiving. Sustained growth can exhaust storage and widen the recovery gap.

panels.title: Time Since Last Successful WAL Archive
panels.description: Can grow normally on an idle database. Interpret alongside WAL generation and ready-to-archive segments. No previous successful archive is omitted, not converted to zero.

Average number of clients queued for a server connection, per pooler. Integrated from PgBouncer's cumulative wait time, so unlike the instantaneous cl_waiting it cannot miss queueing between scrapes. Sustained non-zero means that pool is saturated: every queued client is a round trip waiting on someone else's transaction (database.md section 7).
panels.title: Clients Waiting for a Server

panels.description: Average time a transaction waited for a server connection before it could start, per pooler. This is the latency the pool adds to every query from that pooler's clients.

targets.expr: sum by (pooler) (rate(cnpg_pgbouncer_stats_total_wait_time{namespace=~"$namespace", database="app"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (pooler) (rate(cnpg_pgbouncer_stats_total_xact_count{namespace=~"$namespace", database="app"}[$__rate_interval])) / 1e6

panels.title: Mean Pool Wait per Transaction

panels.description: How long the oldest currently queued client has been waiting, per pooler (the worst pod). A rising line is a queue that is not draining.
panels.title: Longest Client Wait

panels.description: Server connections running a transaction, per pooler, summed over its pods. A flat line at default_pool_size x pods (prod rw: 25 x 2 = 50) is a full pool. rw, api and tasks draw on the primary's max_connections; ro on the replicas'.
panels.title: Server Connections in Use

panels.description: Transactions completed through each pooler. The denominator for the wait panels above: a pool can queue because its clients got slower or because there are more of them.
panels.title: Transactions per Second

panels.description: Actual connections held open against Postgres itself.
panels.title: PostgreSQL Backends
Longest Open Database Transaction
panels.description: Long transactions retain snapshots and occupy pooler slots. Idle-in-transaction sessions are especially useful to investigate.

What client backends on the primary are doing, sampled at each scrape. CPU / Running means executing, not waiting. LWLock WALWrite and IO WALSync are the write path's storage bandwidth; Lock and advisory are row or claim-lock contention; Client ClientRead in an idle in transaction state is a pooler slot held while the client does something else. Check this before optimising anything (database.md, Working rules).

targets.expr: sum by (wait_event_type, wait_event) (cnpg_geoquery_wait_events_backends{namespace=~"$namespace"} and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0))

panels.title: Primary Backends by Wait Event

panels.description: Database queries issued by backend processes only: alias=default uses the primary and alias=replica uses the standby. Views explicitly select the replica for tile geometry and catalog reads; tile visibility resolution stays on the primary. Worker and MCP database activity is not included.
panels.title: Database Queries/sec
Database Errors/sec
panels.description: Backend ORM errors per second. Error series are created lazily; zero is supplied only while a backend exporter is successfully scraped. Missing backend telemetry remains missing.
WAL written by the primary. This is the cluster's write load: every replica replays it and the archiver ships it.
panels.title: WAL Generated

panels.description: All WAL divided by extract tasks completed: the database write cost of one unit of useful work, comparable across throughput levels. It includes the builder's inserts and request builds, so it rises when the builder runs. database.md recorded 2.8-3.9 KB.
panels.title: WAL per Completed Task

panels.description: Full-page images written to WAL per completed task. Each checkpoint makes the next touch of every page log the whole 8 kB page, so this spikes after checkpoints and climbs when they come too often (database.md section 10).
panels.title: Full-Page Images per Completed Task

panels.description: Checkpoints on the primary. timed are the scheduled ones (checkpoint_timeout); requested were forced by WAL volume reaching max_wal_size, and write flat out regardless of checkpoint_completion_target. Requested should stay near zero: a sustained share of them is the self-reinforcing checkpoint/full-page-image loop in database.md section 10.
panels.title: Checkpoints in the Trailing Hour

targets.expr: sum(rate(cnpg_collector_wal_sync_time{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0)) / sum(rate(cnpg_collector_wal_sync{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__rate_interval]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0))

panels.title: Mean WAL Fsync Latency
panels.description: WAL sync time is exported in milliseconds. This is mean latency per fsync, not per transaction; multiple commits can share a sync. Requires track_wal_io_timing.

panels.title: Database Node Disk I/O Latency
panels.description: Mean kernel block-device operation latency on database nodes. Includes other workloads and does not measure remote Ceph/NFS service latency. Database-node selection comes from kube-state-metrics; node-exporter nodename must match the Kubernetes node name.

Rows written per second, summed over partitions. Tasks created is the builder plus request materialization; normal successful processing makes two task updates (claim 0->2, finish 2->1), plus any sweep resets. extract_data rows are processing results. The former Celery extraction flow made three updates per task.
panels.title: Partitioned Table Row Writes

panels.description: Row updates on extract_tasks per completed task. Normal successful processing makes two updates (0->2 claim, 2->1 finish), so the steady-state baseline is about 2. Failures, sweep resets and retries can raise the ratio; chunk timing can cause short-lived variation. The former Celery extraction flow used 0->3->2->1 and had a baseline near 3.
panels.title: extract_tasks Updates per Completed Task

panels.description: Share of extract_tasks updates that were heap-only (rewrote no index entries). Expected to be about zero: status appears in the partial claim index's predicate, which rules HOT out for every status change (database.md section 3). A change here means the index set changed.
panels.title: extract_tasks HOT Update Ratio

panels.description: Bytes of table and index data written out of shared buffers on the primary, by process type. checkpointer and background writer are the normal path. client backend writes mean queries are evicting dirty buffers themselves, on their own time.
panels.title: Primary Relation Writes by Process

panels.description: Heap and index bytes of extract_tasks and extract_data, summed over partitions.
panels.title: Partitioned Table Size

panels.description: Estimated dead row versions, summed over partitions. Every extract_tasks update leaves one behind; this should saw-tooth as autovacuum keeps up, not climb.
panels.title: Dead Rows Awaiting Vacuum

targets.expr: topk(15, sum by (queryid, datname, query) (rate(cnpg_geoquery_statements_exec_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0)))

sum by (queryid, datname, query) (rate(cnpg_geoquery_statements_calls{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0)) and on(queryid, datname, query) topk(15, sum by (queryid, datname, query) (rate(cnpg_geoquery_statements_exec_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0)))

(topk(15, sum by (queryid, datname, query) (rate(cnpg_geoquery_statements_exec_seconds{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0)))) / (sum by (queryid, datname, query) (rate(cnpg_geoquery_statements_calls{namespace=~"$namespace"}[$__range]) and on(namespace, pod) (cnpg_pg_replication_in_recovery{namespace=~"$namespace"} == 0))) * 1000

panels.title: Top Statements on the Primary
panels.description: The statements with the most cumulative execution time on the primary over the selected range, from pg_stat_statements. Load is execution seconds per second: the average number of backends busy running that statement. Only each instance's current top 20 is exported, so a statement new to the list shows less than its full range. Rows retain query ID and database identity because the displayed SQL text is truncated to 160 characters and distinct statements can share that prefix.
Two baselines here are by design, not faults: GET on request-list-create always returns 404, and 429s on it are RequestSubmitThrottle doing its job. Everything else is worth looking at.

targets.expr:
# 4xx by endpoint (client errors - may indicate API misuse)
sum by (view) (rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{namespace=~"$namespace", status=~"4.."}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.title: 4XX Errors By View

targets.expr:
# 5xx by endpoint (server errors - actionable)
sum by (view) (rate(django_http_responses_total_by_status_view_method_total{namespace=~"$namespace", status=~"5.."}[$__rate_interval]))

panels.description: Excludes boundary tiles, Explore, request creation and exports — each of which is slow enough to swamp the sitewide figure. They have their own panels.

panels.title: General Latency (no tiles or heavy endpoints)

panels.description: All tile responses are HTTP 200 — an unresolvable or unauthorized fc_name returns an empty body, not a 404 — so the response-code panels below cannot see tile failures. Latency and volume are the signals here.
panels.title: Tile Requests/sec

panels.description: Served from pre-simplified matviews (features_simplified_z0_5 / z6_9 / z10_12) below z13 and from the raw features table above it, so the spread across these percentiles is largely a zoom-tier mix, not variance within one query.

# P50 - median response time
histogram_quantile(0.50,
  sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", view="features:feature-collection-tiles"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le)
) * 1000

# P95 - captures most user experience
histogram_quantile(0.95,
  sum(rate(django_http_requests_latency_seconds_by_view_method_bucket{namespace=~"$namespace", view="features:feature-collection-tiles"}[$__rate_interval])) by (le)

panels.title: Tile Latency

panels.description: Share of tile requests served within each threshold. Thresholds are real django-prometheus bucket edges; changing them to a value that is not a bucket edge yields an empty series.
panels.title: Tile Latency SLO

panels.description: The zoom tiers hit different matviews and cannot be separated by label — django-prometheus keys on the view name, and z is a URL kwarg. They do separate visually here: distinct horizontal bands are the tiers, and a band drifting upward is one matview degrading. A single smeared band instead of bands usually means user-upload collections, which simplify per request rather than reading a matview.
panels.title: Tile Latency Distribution

panels.description: All database queries issued by backend processes through the replica alias. Includes boundary tiles, dataset catalog and coverage reads, boundary autocomplete, and public API reads. Compare with tile volume for context; ordinary browsing also contributes to this series. Worker and MCP queries are not included.
panels.title: Replica Queries/sec

panels.description: Ad-hoc dataset exploration — the heaviest read path outside tiles.

# P50 - median response time
histogram_quantile(0.50,
